title: Graph-Structured Random-Effects Dependence in Linear Mixed Models: Covariance and Precision Graphs
content: Linear mixed models represent cluster-specific heterogeneity through a random-effects covariance matrix, but dependence among random coefficients is rarely modeled explicitly. We propose a graph-structured framework in which random-effect components are vertices and two complementary graphs encode marginal dependence through covariance zeros and conditional dependence through precision-matrix zeros. Scale-invariant correlation and partial-correlation weights are screened by a vanishing threshold, and selected covariance graphs may be refitted by restricted maximum likelihood. We establish Gaussian independence semantics, invariance to diagonal rescaling, support consistency under standard REML consistency and beta-min conditions, and a perturbation bound linking covariance sparsification to the marginal covariance of the observations. In 500 Monte Carlo replications per configuration with three random effects, exact support recovery increased from 0.612 to 0.930 for covariance graphs and from 0.470 to 0.950 for precision graphs as the number of clusters increased from 30 to 120. With five random effects and 120 clusters, edge sensitivity and specificity ranged from 0.895 to 0.923, although exact whole-graph recovery was lower. A Grunfeld-panel application illustrates threshold sensitivity, borderline edge decisions, and graph-guided covariance simplification with nearly unchanged fixed-effect estimates. The framework separates random-effect inclusion from dependence-structure selection.
